prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: I keep B038 as a single-topic prize for Buchwald and Hartwig. After round 1 nothing about the science has been challenged: ligand-controlled Pd catalysis made aryl C-N bond formation general, the mechanism (oxidative addition, amine binding, the hard amido-palladium reductive elimination) is supported by independent structural and kinetic work, and thirty years of use in medicinal, process and materials chemistry leave no maturity question. Attribution is the cleanest of any shortlisted achievement: two independent groups, two names, and no need to leave out a decisive contributor. The chair asked what these two enabled that the 2010 laureates did not. My answer is that amines, amides and N-heterocycles could not be coupled with aryl halides in a general, predictable way before the dialkylbiarylphosphine and hindered-alkylphosphine ligand families existed, because the C-N reductive elimination step needed its own ligand design and not simply the C-C coupling toolkit. Kosugi's tin-amide chemistry was a real precursor, but it needed toxic stoichiometric tin reagents and had narrow scope, so the citation should say 'development of palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling' and the discussion can acknowledge Kosugi and Migita without crediting them.
statement.case_against: The 2010 prize on palladium cross-coupling is a serious objection: Aqvist, Aili, Brzezinski, Chabes and Linke all raised it, and several members weigh a new principle above an extension of an honoured one. My preferred option is a method, not a new concept, and it has only two first-place supporters, so it could stall short of five votes while B066 gathers support. If the committee concludes that 2010 closed the field, I would not defend B038 against a candidate that is both new in principle and well attributed. Kosugi's priority also remains a point a critic could press.

responses.point: The chair, now ranking B066 first, argues that the committee should recognise the established principle and not wait for an approved degrader, and that ternary-complex structures, cereblon biochemistry and many independent programmes establish it.
responses.response: I accept the distinction between discovery and product and I withdraw the idea that approval is a requirement. The mechanism is reproduced, and that is the right test. My objection is now only attribution. Your own case-against says Handa's cereblon work is a molecular-glue story that is not the PROTAC concept, and Ciulli's VHL ligands and structures are what made degraders drug-like. If the committee cannot say whether the citation honours PROTACs, glues or both, and who stands behind each, then it would be a prize I could not defend as precisely as Buchwald and Hartwig. I keep B066 as my first alternative, and if the vote moves there I would want the citation to state the mechanistic principle explicitly and not the thalidomide history, as you and Chabes propose.

responses.point: Johan values the simplicity of C-N coupling but expects colleagues to call it an extension of the 2010 prize, and he prefers sequencing by synthesis as overdue and highly consequential.
responses.response: On the 2010 overlap, the test I apply is whether the new work needed a new idea. It did. C-N bond formation required ligands that make the amido-palladium complex reductively eliminate, which is a different mechanistic problem from transmetalation-driven C-C coupling. On B057 I agree about impact and maturity and I now list it as my second alternative. My doubt is what the citation would celebrate. Sequencing by synthesis combines surface chemistry, terminator nucleotides, optics and engineering, and the Rothberg, Mayer and Ju claims make the priority record hard to cut to two or three names without an argument that the chemistry is the core. I would want a precise citation before voting for it, and I do not think the committee has reached that.

responses.point: Peter prefers B023 for Gray and Winkler as a physically stated mechanism with a compact pair, and says he weighs a new fundamental mechanism above an extension of an existing method.
responses.response: I share your wish for physical clarity, and the Gray-Winkler pair is compact and well confirmed. I would put the question differently. A new mechanism is one kind of Nobel achievement, and a method that lets a whole community do what it could not before is another, and the committee has honoured both. My concern with B023 is that Marcus theory (1992) and the Dutton-Moser and Beratan-Onuchic work make the priority and scope question harder than for B038, and no other member ranked it. I would ask whether you would carry your vote to B038 or B057 if B023 cannot build support. I would take B038 over B066 on attribution, though I understand you do not rank it high.

responses.point: Andrei sees B038 as having clean attribution and no maturity problem but reads it as an extension of the 2010 idea, and he keeps B066 first, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa and the argument that Ciulli's work is optimisation.
responses.response: I agree that attribution and maturity are not the issue for B038, and that we differ on novelty. On B066, I find your argument that Ciulli optimised a concept less settled than you suggest. Making a degrader work in practice required VHL ligands and the ternary-complex structures, which are structural and chemical results and are the evidence I would want to see credited, because that is where the structural basis of the mechanism was shown. That is why I read the three-name limit as the real problem for B066, not the timing.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat the 2010 cross-coupling prize as already covering C-N coupling, which is the main reason B038 might not reach five votes.
Whether B066 can be given a defensible three-name attribution across the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands and the VHL structural work, and if it can, I would move to it.
Whether the sequencing case (B057) can be reduced to a chemically precise citation with a defensible set of names.
Whether acknowledging Kosugi and Migita in the discussion is enough to answer the priority question.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1 and no recusal needed. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, which does not involve any shortlisted candidate. I have no tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or any other credited person, and electron crystallography is not represented on the shortlist.
